title: Poppler: TIFF predictor bit-shift exponent undefined behavior
ai_system: Revelio using Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: UC Berkeley Revelio research team and affected project maintainers
summary: The Revelio paper identifies a integer overflow / undefined behavior in Poppler v26.04.0: tiff predictor bit-shift exponent undefined behavior. It lists the author-assessed severity as Moderate and says the finding was manually validated with a reproducible sanitizer-backed proof of vulnerability through a reachable project test harness. This is Table V item 5 of the seven-project real-world hunt.
ai_role: The paper describes Revelio as using Claude Haiku 4.5 for hypothesis generation and Claude Sonnet 4.6 for proof-of-vulnerability confirmation; its experimental-method section says this configuration was used for the seven-project OSS-Fuzz hunt. The authors state all 19 tabled findings were manually validated and sanitizer-confirmed. The paper does not provide a per-item model trajectory, so the exact division of Claude work within this row is not independently stated.
classification_note: The paper publicly identifies this distinct finding on 2026-06-20. The authors describe the hunt as searching for previously unknown flaws, but this record does not assert exploitation in the wild or operational zero-day status.
remediation_note: The Revelio paper reports the issue as fixed after validation and disclosure; no public item-level vendor advisory or CVE mapping was verified.

impacts.conditions: The sanitizer-backed paper identifies undefined behavior in the TIFF predictor bit-shift exponent; it states no downstream effect.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.
